1.say: Push the thin white power wire into a free five-hole row near the top edge. Push the thin blue power wire into another free five-hole row to the right.
placements: thin white insulated power wire with stripped bare end for one battery feed → top edge five-hole row of the white mini breadboard on the left side of the frame, pushed fully in by fingers with wire standing up; in the video: white wire standing up from top edge left of blue wire, printed numbers not readable and the video does not show which row; match the picture and keep separate from blue wire row

thin blue insulated power wire with stripped bare end for the other battery feed → different top edge five-hole row of the same white mini breadboard a few holes to the right of the white wire on the right side of the frame, pushed fully in by fingers with wire standing up; in the video: blue wire standing up from top edge right of white wire, printed numbers not readable and the video does not show which row; match the picture
watch_for: Both wires in the same five-hole row create a battery short; the light will never glow and the wires or batteries may feel warm.
Wire pushed in only partly makes no contact; if the wire wiggles or falls out the circuit will stay dark.
1.check_yourself: The white breadboard sits on the table with a white wire and a blue wire standing up from its top edge in separate rows.
1.safety: Keep the bare ends of the white and blue wires apart so they never touch.

2.say: Push one silver leg of the small blue resistor into the white wire row. Push the other silver leg into a free five-hole row to the right.
placements: small blue body resistor with two thin silver legs, 220 ohm current limiter from narration → left leg in same top edge five-hole row as white wire and right leg in a free five-hole row a few holes to the right, body lying flat across the top of the white mini breadboard near the top edge, pushed in by fingers; in the video: resistor lying across top of board, printed numbers not readable and the video does not show which row; match the picture
watch_for: Both resistor legs in the same five-hole row bypass the resistor; the light may glow very bright or burn out instead of glowing normally.
Resistor leg missing the white wire row leaves an open circuit; if the light stays dark the leg is probably in the wrong row.
2.check_yourself: A small blue banded resistor lies across the top of the white breadboard with its legs in separate rows.

3.say: Push the short leg of the blue dome light into the resistor row. Push the long leg into the same five-hole row as the blue wire.
placements: small blue dome LED with long leg anode plus side and short leg with flat side cathode minus side → short leg in same five-hole row as right leg of resistor toward the negative feed and long leg in same five-hole row as blue power wire toward the positive feed, body standing upright on right side of white mini breadboard facing up, pushed in by fingers until seated and glowing blue when powered; in the video: blue LED upright on right side of board, printed numbers not readable and the video does not show which row; match the picture
watch_for: Light reversed with long and short legs swapped blocks current; if the light stays dark the long leg is probably in the wrong row.
Both light legs in the same five-hole row short the light; the light will stay dark even though power is connected.
3.check_yourself: The blue LED stands upright on the white breadboard glowing blue.
